before.story: California Governor Gavin Newsom Commutes State's 548 Death Row Sentences
before.summary: In one of his final executive acts before concluding his eight-year tenure, California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole. The historic decree eliminates approximately one-quarter of all U.S. capital punishment sentences, drawing sharp rebukes from political figures such as Donald Trump and vocal vows from local prosecutors to continue seeking the death penalty.

after.story: California Governor Gavin Newsom Commutes State's 548 Death Row Sentences

note: A formal lawsuit challenges Governor Newsom's commutation decree over alleged failures to properly notify district attorneys.
